member.name: T:C1.Pdf.C1PdfDocument
member.summary: Provides methods to create and save PDF documents.

remarks.para: When you create an instance of the class, you get a PDF document with a single blank page. You can then add content to the page using methods similar to those available in the .NET Graphics class (DrawRectangle, DrawString, etc.).
You can add new pages using the method, and select the page size using the or properties.
When the document is ready, you can save it to a file or a stream using the method.
The coordinate system used by is based on points, with the origin located at the top left corner of the page. You can retrieve the page rectangle (measured in points) using the property.

member.name: P:C1.Pdf.C1PdfDocument.CurrentPage
member.summary: Gets or sets the index of the current page within the document.

remarks.para: The property determines which page of the document should receive the output from the methods that generate content (e.g. DrawString method).
The value is an integer ranging from -1 (no active page) to . Count - 1.

You rarely have to use the property while creating a document. When a object is created, a blank page is automatically added and becomes the current page, so you can immediately start adding content to it. When the method is invoked, a new page is added to the document and becomes the current page.
The property is useful when you want to reopen pages that have already been generated and add content to them (for example, page headers and footers).

member.name: M:C1.Pdf.C1PdfDocument.AddLink(System.String,System.Drawing.RectangleF)
member.summary: Adds a hyperlink to the current page.
member.param: Link destination (can be a Url, a file name, or a local link destination).
Area on the page that will behave as a link (expressed in points, from the top-left corner of the page).

member.name: M:C1.Pdf.C1PdfDocument.AddLink(System.String,System.Int32,System.Drawing.RectangleF)
member.summary: Adds a hyperlink to the document.
member.param: Link destination (can be a Url, a file name, or a local link destination).
Index of the page that contains the hyperlink
Area on the page that will behave as a link (expressed in points, from the top-left corner of the page).

remarks.para: Hyperlinks can be external (Urls and file names) or local (other locations within the same document).

Local links are useful when you want to implement some type of cross-referencing within the document, such as a table of contents or an index. Local links are identical to regular hyperlinks, except for two things:
1) The parameter must start with a "#", and
2) You must specify the target location for the link using the AddTarget method.

Note that the AddLink method does not add any visible content to the page, so you will usually need another command along with AddLink to specify some text or an image that the user can see, as the example below demonstrates.

member.example:
The code below adds a string that says "Visit site" and a link that takes the user to the ComponentOne home page:
Rect rc = new Rect(50, 50, 100, 15); // RectangleF Font font = new Font("Arial", 10, PdfFontStyle.Underline); // FontStyle _c1pdf.AddLink("http://www.google.com", rc); _c1pdf.DrawString("Visit site", font, Color.Blue, rc); // Brushes.Blue

member.name: T:C1.Pdf.PdfSecurity
member.summary: Provides security and encryption services and manages permissions for objects.

remarks.para: has properties that allow you to specify owner and user passwords for a Pdf document. The is required to change passwords and permissions. The is required to open the document.
also has properties that allow you to specify what permissions a regular user should have. For example, you may allow users to see the document but not to print or edit it.
You can specify permissions and set only the , leaving the empty. In this case, anyone will be allowed to open the document, but only the owner will be allowed to change the permissions.

Note that the encryption scheme used by Pdf is public and is not 100% secure. There are ways to crack encrypted Pdf documents. The security provided is adequate to protect your documents from most casual attacks, but if your data is truly sensitive you should not rely on Pdf encryption alone.
